title: Finiteness of the concrete strict-hensel root normalization
statement: Let $i:U\to L$ be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $G$ a finite group and $W\to U$ a finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. Let $R$ be a commutative regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], $\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}R\to L$, and $f\in R$ a nonzerodivisor with $R/(f)$ regular. Suppose $|G|$ is a unit in $R$. Assume $\beta:U\times_L\operatorname{Spec}R\cong D(f)$ commutes with the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point], $H$ its canonical strict henselization coordinate-ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], and $b:R\to H$ a map inducing its structural morphism [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Put $g=b(f)$, $n_0=|G|$, $A=H[T]/(T^{n_0}-g)$, $N=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $q:N\to\operatorname{Spec}H$ the algebra structural morphism, and $V=D(g)\subset N$. Assume $g$ is not a unit. Suppose $N$ is locally Noetherian. Let $p:W\times_L V\to V$ be the second pullback projection along $V\hookrightarrow N\xrightarrow{q}\operatorname{Spec}H\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Spec}b}\operatorname{Spec}R\xrightarrow{\varphi}L$, and assume $p$ is finite and etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Put $a=p\circ(V\hookrightarrow N)$ and let $a^\nu:C_a\to N$ be its concrete relative normalization [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization], defined affine locally by integral closure in the sections of the source of $a$. Then $a^\nu$ is finite. No etaleness at the divisor or identification over $V$ is asserted.

proof.text: First transport the retained upstream regular-divisor quotient theorem from the full affine-neighbourhood colimit to H through smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso. The theorem smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso_toBase identifies the structural maps. Pull the nonunit condition back through the inverse ring equivalence. Transfer Noetherianity by isNoetherianRing_of_ringEquiv and the quotient properties by Ideal.quotientEquiv, IsRegularRing.of_ringEquiv and MulEquiv.isDomain_iff. Use strictHenselizationLocalStructure to make H local. The regular-divisor quotient theorem gives Noetherianness of H and regularity of H/(g). To recover flatness on the original small coordinate-ring colimit without importing the conflicting upstream structural-map helper, form the natural stage maps GammaSpecIso(R).inv followed by each pointed etale neighbourhood structure map on global sections. Cofilteredness of the pointed category makes the opposite ring diagram filtered. The stage maps are flat since etale morphisms are flat. The characterizing equation of exists_strictHenselizationStructuralMap and Spec.map_injective identify every composite with its colimit coprojection with b. Apply RingHom.Flat.of_isColimit, the colimit-presentation form of the ind-flat characterization, and then hf.of_flat to make g regular.

Specialize Mathlib AdjoinRoot.eval₂_root and simplify polynomial evaluation to obtain t^|G|=g; no duplicate root-relation theorem is declared. Construct the ring equivalence A/(t) with H/(g) using AdjoinRoot.lift and the quotient universal property in both directions; verify the maps are inverse on coefficients and the root. Monicity gives that A is finite free over H. Every maximal ideal of A contracts to the maximal ideal of the local H by integrality, hence contains g and t. Maximal ideals of A therefore correspond to those of the local quotient A/(t), so A is local.

Apply RootAlgebraRegularAtRoot to the maximal ideal of A, which contains t. Its prime localization is regular local. All its denominators are units because A is local, so IsLocalization.atUnits identifies this localization with A.

RegularLocalLocalization makes A a regular ring. RegularRingNormal supplies normal domain prime localizations; identify them with the stalks of N through Spec.stalkIso. Regular locality also gives that A is a domain, so N is integral. It is Noetherian by the supplied local Noetherian hypothesis and affineness.

Package p as a finite etale object over V and apply finiteEtale_open_integralClosure_finite on every affine open B of N. This produces the finite module defining the relative normalization in that affine chart.

Mathlib fromNormalization_app and normalizationObjIso identify the section map of the normalization with this finite structural algebra map followed by a ring isomorphism. The IsFinite constructor with these affine section maps proves the conclusion.

theorem GaloisCover.strict_hensel_root_normalization_finite
    {L U : Scheme.{u}} (i : U ⟶ L)
    (G : Type (u + 1)) [Group G] [Finite G] (W : GaloisCover G U)
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (φ : Spec R ⟶ L) (f : R)
    (_hG : IsUnit (Nat.card G : R))
    [IsRegularRing R] (hf : IsSMulRegular R f)
    [IsRegularRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span {f})]
    (β : pullback i φ ≅ Scheme.Opens.toScheme (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f))
    (_hβ : β.hom ≫ Scheme.Opens.ι (X := Spec R) (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f) = pullback.snd i φ)
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (barY : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R)
    (b : R ⟶ strictHenselizationRing barY)
    (hb : Spec.map b = strictHenselizationStructuralMap barY) :
    let H := strictHenselizationRing barY
    let g := b.hom f
    let A := AdjoinRoot ((Polynomial.X : Polynomial H) ^ Nat.card G - Polynomial.C g)
    let N := Spec (CommRingCat.of A)
    let q := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap H A))
    let V : N.Opens := PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen (algebraMap H A g)
    ¬ IsUnit g → ∀ (hN : IsLocallyNoetherian N),
    letI := hN
    let p := pullback.snd (W.π ≫ i) (V.ι ≫ q ≫ Spec.map b ≫ φ)
    ∀ (hp : IsFinite p),
    letI := hp
    let a := p ≫ V.ι
    Etale p → IsFinite a.fromNormalization
